summary: Tansen Sen works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, among others. He taught history at Baruch College (1997–2017) and became Professor at NYU Shanghai in 2017.
Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and he founded Kangien in 1801.

Tanuja Ajotikar specializes in Indology and computational linguistics. She held posts at Harvard University, Maharishi Vedic University as Co-director of Sanskrit Department India Programs, and the Sanskrit Library as Assistant Professor (attested 2024–2025).

Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He served at the Ministry of Religion (1872–1874), the University of Tokyo (1879), and as superintendent at Komazawa University (1891).
Tao Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2017–2026). In 2026, he was a Postdoctoral Fellow at Fo Guang Shan.

Tao Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and served as an Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan works in Indology and linguistics. He completed a BA at Fudan University in 2010 and earned a Magister Artium at the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. At Emory University, she served as a lecturer in religious studies and director of the Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003) and became Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Tarapada Chowdhury (1907–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Succeeding Edward Hamilton Johnston by 1950, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Patna College (attested 1950).
Tara Sheemar is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2011 and became an Associate Professor at Janki Devi Memorial College in 2003.
Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1962–1978) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen (~1962–1998).

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812–1885) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University (~1845–1872) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Benares Sanskrit College.

Tariq Rafeeq Khan is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Jiwaji University (2017–2020) and became an assistant professor at the Islamic University of Science and Technology in 2022.

Taro Tokutake works in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at Hiroshima University and Kyoto University (PhD 2024), he held visiting postdoctoral fellowships at CNRS (2024–2025), Paris Cité University (2025–2026), and the University of Edinburgh (2026), lecturing at Kyoto in 2024.

Tarthang Tulku is a scholar and teacher of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Tarthang Monastery, taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), and founded the Nyingma Institute in 1972, serving as its head.
Tashi Densapa is a Tibetologist and historian. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978, 2002) and as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 2008).

Tashi Rabgey is a Tibetologist who studied at University College Toronto, Cambridge, Harvard, and Magdalen College. She has held posts at Georgetown University and the University of Virginia, where she was co-director of the Tibet Center.

Tashi Samphel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and linguistics. He was a research officer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1995), director of the Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), and professor at CIHTS (attested 2014–2019).
